produces: New datasets added to the inventory, each with licence, years, unit and access checked; duds ruled out so nobody re-checks them
why: Grows the inventory; this is the biggest pool of unexplored leads
basis: iterations 20 and 22: about 27 rows per hour, 8 requests per row, 200 families gave 32 rows; tokens not measured; the 11-18 test session took about 1 min each for 3 that were all ruled out
rate_note: measured on the best-ranked leads; the rest may give fewer

produces: Unverified (Bronze) datasets become verified: licence, years, spatial unit and access read from the publisher's page with the link kept
why: Turns listed-but-unchecked datasets into ones people can rely on
basis: page reads on 10-22 and 10-28: 431 rows, about 7M tokens (15-17k per row), brief budget 2-3 min per row

produces: Datasets on sites that block scripts get checked by you in your browser; Claude only writes down what you report
why: No script or AI can do these; costs your time, not tokens
basis: iteration 18: 145 of 167 opened; minutes are a person's, a guess

produces: Dead or moved datasets get their new address, or are confirmed retired
why: Keeps the inventory honest about what still exists
basis: iteration 19: 14 of 28 resolved; time and tokens not measured; the 11-18 test session took 6 min, 4 requests and a search for one item

produces: Datasets counted as verified on thin evidence get their missing checks filled in; some reach Gold
why: 97 'verified' datasets have at most two of the four core checks settled, so the verified total overstates what we know
basis: same page-read measurements as 'read'; the rate is a guess; the 11-18 test session took 4.5 min and 3.5 fetches per item

produces: For a verified dataset: its column list, the place-key column, which geography and vintage that key is (e.g. 2020 census tracts), and its geometry
result_label: datasets with their place key recorded
why: These are the inputs a Gaia recipe needs; only 10 datasets state their key vintage so far
basis: iteration 25: 85 rows, 68 requests, about 10 min; tokens not measured; the 11-18 test session took 12 min for one item with a hard-to-read metadata file
rate_note: measured on easier datasets than the ones left; expect fewer
